items.desc: Survey published in Lancet reveals ‘hormonal hesitancy’ on the rise – with implants and injections also increasingly spurned The number of young women using hormonal contraception fell drastically in the past decade, with social media fuelling the “hormonal hesitancy” phenomenon. New findings from the fourth national survey of sexual attitudes and lifestyles (Natsal-4), published in The Lancet, found that almost one in five women in Great Britain at risk of unintended pregnancy were not using effective contraception. items.title: Faulty electrical goods returned to UK supermarkets ending up on Ghana ‘megadump’

The faulty electrical appliances, including toasters and slow cookers, had been returned to major UK supermarkets. They were found at Agbogbloshie, one of the world’s largest e-waste sites, in Ghana’s capital, Accra, a joint investigation by Unearthed and Greenpeace Africa has found.
